svg.title: The Dubstack lifecycle: setup, two on-ramps into the basecamp goal loop, and the work between features
svg.desc: Start, before the first project: orchestration-setup decides which model owns which work, and stack-preferences holds your preferred technologies. Project context, in any order: project-home for the home, brand-skill-generator for the brand, and design-interview or conversational-interview for requirements, the glossary and brainstorming. On-ramp for a new project: 1 context, 2 architecture with design-interview, 3 reference sources with upstream-source, 4 scaffolding with project-scaffolding, which opens a goal, 5 the first major goal, 6 follow-up goals. On-ramp for an existing codebase: 1 context with project-home and the brand, 2 safeguards with project-scaffolding as a goal, 3 architecture-review, whose candidates become goals, 4 features as goals. Both on-ramps feed goals into basecamp, the front door for any work, which picks the route by what remains unresolved: do it now, research, design-interview (a design discussion, or a PRD then a TDD), structure-outline, implement-outline, describe-pr, babysit-pr, and done once merged. After each stage the work returns to basecamp, which records it and hands off the next stage. Between features, architecture-review, reference updates through upstream-source, dependency pull requests through babysit-pr, and issues feed new goals back to basecamp. Anywhere: research, babysit-pr, visualize-html, svg-design, skill-writing. The guide, dubstack, reads where a project stands and names the next step.
